rationale: C04 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child’s operative paragraph. Both proclamations move from recitals establishing the occasion’s public significance to a presidential invitation for participation and a request or invitation that the Governors of the States, Territories, and possessions issue supporting proclamations. C04 is materially closer than C07 and C12 in wording and proximity, although those earlier annual proclamations exhibit the same machinery. The shared proclamation closing is boilerplate and is not relied upon.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby invite American citizens from every region of our country to come to their Nation's Capital and participate in the sesquicentennial observances.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I also urge the medical profession, the press, the radio and motion-picture industries, and all interested agencies and individuals to unite during April 1950 in public dedication to a program for the control of cancer.
shared_material.explanation: Both use the operative proclamation to invite or urge broad public and organizational participation in the designated observance.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I also request the Governors of the respective States, Territories and possessions of the United States to issue proclamations urging participation in these celebrations.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I invite the Governors of the States, Territories, and possessions of the United States to issue proclamations for the same purpose.
shared_material.explanation: This is a close and distinctive match in administrative machinery and phrasing: an appeal to the same set of governors to issue proclamations supporting the national observance.
